correctness.rationale: For all r>=2,s>=1 the update of each part is determined exactly by total one-count minus its own count, with tie preserving the entire part. A homogeneous part cannot become mixed, so periodic mixed parts must all tie and have equal populations t. Their homogeneous companions swap; conservation forces equal full and empty counts and (k-1)(2t-s)=0. This is exhaustive and yields the exact labelled constant-term coefficient and one-mixed-part correction; the only additional fixed states are r half-filled parts. From any starting state, one update leaves only equal-population mixed parts plus homogeneous parts; a second step either erases all mixed parts or swaps homogeneous parts, which ensures periodicity by update three. The explicit population path (0,3,3,3,4) -> (5,3,3,3,0) -> (0,5,5,5,5) -> (5,5,5,5,5) proves global sharpness. Stirling and Laplace arguments yield the two asymptotic regimes. The included checker re-evaluates 167116 labelled states across 20 (r,s) parameter pairs, using independent vertex-level and occupancy models, and directly checks \(F^5=F^3\); finite checks are corroboration, not the all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: The natural invariant is the full labelled attractor census and global convergence speed for regular Turán-type graphs. The result supplies all r,s fixed and two-cycle counts, exact zeta information, and a sharp finite time cutoff. Its key mechanism, one exceptional mixed tie class when r is odd versus half-filled mixed classes in all other cases, creates a quantitatively nontrivial polynomial-prefactor phase difference for odd s and a different exponential base for even s. This new all-number-of-parts phase diagram is not a mere fixed-parameter table and is useful for comparing collective oscillation capacity in regular multipartite opinion networks; r=3 and the generic period-two property are acknowledged rather than counted as new.
